msi.inspection: Read-only Windows Installer database queries; not installed or executed

hazards: CheckIfAppIsRunning invokes KillProcessCurrentUser by executable basename
PageLeaveReinstall can invoke a shipped old uninstaller before NSIS_HOOK_PREINSTALL
Stock uninstall removes a productName Run value without ownership verification

integration.runtimeGate: check_predecessor errors must pause every setter; recheck must call check_predecessor again
integration.startup: Only this module's checked startup APIs may change startup; remove generic autostart plugin mutation access
integration.canonicalAutostartPatch: Under the root config_actions lock, use apply_autostart_change(enable) -> AutostartChange; commit ConfigManager.patch; consume the receipt with rollback() on commit failure, or drop it after success. The receipt holds the native startup mutex. The equivalent configure_autostart_with_commit(enable, commit) helper is also available. Never use configure_autostart(previous_bool) as rollback.
integration.startupRollback: The helper records successful or readback-confirmed Run edits, verifies effective state before the supplied canonical commit, and on failure restores exact prior bytes only where live values still match that transaction; it never rewrites StartupApproved. Preflight refusal performs no rollback writes. configure_autostart commits this same checked transaction by discarding its successful receipt.
integration.nsisUninstallRemoval: After the existing ownership/startup preflight, prepare checked, no-overwrite recovery copies of both the registered main executable and uninstall.exe outside the auto-cleaned plugin directory. Delete resources and sidecars before the cleanup pair; check each Delete error and native absence separately, including uninstall.exe. Missing non-helper payloads are idempotent, but missing registered cleanup executables still fail the existing preflight. Any removal or readback failure exits nonzero before shortcuts or installation metadata are removed, restores only missing cleanup executables without overwriting replacements, and retains the recovery directory with explicit partial-removal instructions. Restoration exclusively creates a private directory under INSTDIR on the installation volume, copies complete bytes there without overwriting, then publishes by same-volume MoveFileExW(flags=0). TEMP=C: and installation=E: remain automatically recoverable; no partial registered executable, replacement, or cross-volume rename-copy fallback is allowed. Only the owned, empty staging directory is removed; partial or locked staging is retained and reported. If actual access or lock errors prevent restoration, restore only missing original paths from the complete recovery copies (not .restore staging files) before retrying; an in-place installer cannot bypass missing ownership paths. On success, move the recovery directory into the private plugin directory for normal NSIS temporary-file cleanup before removing metadata. Never use reboot deletion, broad recursive removal, or the NSIS _?= in-place mode to claim successful removal.

handoffVerification.nsis: Source/configuration verified; current-user same-format in-place template compiles with the pinned Tauri CLI. Compilation is not installation or upgrade validation; disposable-VM handoff remains a mandatory release gate.
handoffVerification.msi: Published v1.0.5 database and pinned bundler verified; the new template compiles with immediate synchronous preflight plus DisableShutdown. The custom-action process must prove the initiating interactive SID/session. If Windows executes it in SYSTEM/session 0 or an alternate account, it intentionally blocks; elevated/standard-user VM verification is mandatory before claiming MSI upgrade support.
handoffVerification.buildConfiguration: Debug installer compilation only. No generated installer has been installed or exercised.
ifMsiInteractiveContextCannotBeProven: Do not ship the MSI as an automatic orderly-upgrade path.
Keep the format decision explicit: implement and validate a separately signed interactive bootstrapper/MSI handoff, or obtain product approval to defer MSI releases.
Do not silently switch targets from all or treat UI confirmation as proof of predecessor exit.

supportedBoundary: Both shipped installer formats remain enabled
Same-format, same-directory upgrade for the signed-in interactive shell user
Exact registered executable path plus token SID and interactive session; no basename-only ownership
An installer also refuses replacement of registered files in use by another user/session, without requesting or forcing that user's termination
Retry/Cancel asks the user to Quit/Exit through the tray; silent/passive failure never kills a process
Cross-format migration, changed installation directory, SYSTEM installs and alternate-account elevation are explicitly blocked
Registered startup only; enabling autostart from a portable/development copy is refused
Windows Startup Apps disable overrides are preserved, not rewritten
A Windows-disabled legacy Run entry remains quoted at the same replaced executable path; migration to the specific name waits until Windows enables it
An orphaned disabled approval under the specific startup name is not overwritten without ownership evidence and requires Windows startup-registration repair
Startup changes are verified per value, not atomic with installer rollback or app config
After an interrupted upgrade, a confirmed stable startup entry may still launch the unchanged predecessor

A failed NSIS uninstall may already have retired owned startup and removed earlier resources; it retains ownership metadata, restores missing cleanup executables where possible, and keeps exact recovery copies for retry/manual repair without overwriting unrelated replacements
The Run registry API has no compare-and-swap; external concurrent writes after the final precheck remain a Windows limitation
A later manually launched standalone or installed v1 copy is outside the orderly handoff guarantee
releaseValidationGates: Build both templates with the pinned Tauri CLI and run Rust pure/mocked tests
Verify installer_command executes before all Tauri/config/controller initialization
Disposable-VM NSIS/MSI upgrades with a running v1 tray controller: Retry must block until actual exit
Verify an unrelated same-name process and unrelated generic Run entry remain untouched
Verify a different interactive account is not targeted; test standard and same-user elevated MSI
Verify full, passive and silent installer paths, fresh installs, repair, failed startup migration and uninstall

Lock only the existing NSIS uninstall.exe in a disposable VM: failed WriteUninstaller must abort before publishing new metadata, success callbacks, or application launch; the user is warned not to use the old uninstaller

During NSIS uninstall in a disposable VM, lock each payload type and uninstall.exe after preflight: require nonzero failure before shortcut/metadata removal, retained or restored cleanup executables, and explicit recovery instructions if restoration is denied. TEMP=C: with installation=E: must restore automatically through installation-volume staging. Retry must work after closing locks; missing non-helper files are idempotent. Verify normal self-copy and _?= failure, silent/passive/full UI, preserved unrelated files, and successful cleanup of both registered executables
Inspect generated NSIS and MSI artifacts for any unexpected close/kill or Restart Manager shutdown path
Verify next logon starts only the upgraded controller and preserves an existing Windows-disabled startup choice
Re-review metadata identities and template inputs whenever the bundler, publisher, binary name, scope or formats change
